                    ### Question
                    Question linked to image # 15 While we are exploring this patient, he has a sudden worsening of his hemodynamic state and an increase in his tachypnea.                     ### Options
                    opa. Progression of the right pulmonary contusion.
opb. Expansive right cervical vascular injury.
opc. Cardiac tamponade.
opd. Right hemothorax
ope. Tension pneumothorax.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely diagnosis in this case is tension pneumothorax, supported by the presence of tracheal deviation to the left, distended jugular veins, absence of ventilation in the right hemithorax, sudden worsening of hemodynamic state, and increase in tachypnea. These clinical findings are consistent with tension pneumothorax, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate intervention.
